name: Sudhanshu "Suds" Jain
title: Santa Clara City Councilmember, District 5
background: Jain represents District 5 on the Santa Clara City Council. He is the filer and lead author of the primary argument in favor of Measure C, the November 2026 City Charter amendment raising the Council-approval threshold for public-works contracts from $1,000 to $250,000 and authorizing 'best value' contracting methods such as design-build. Full detail on the measure itself, including the Impartial Analysis, fiscal narrative, and the arguments for and against, is covered in content/measures/scc-measure-c-2026.json and not duplicated here.

Per San José Spotlight's coverage of the measure, Jain was the councilmember who pushed to separate the public-works procurement changes from a much larger, ultimately abandoned comprehensive City Charter overhaul that a 13-member Charter Review Committee had spent over a year developing. Jain is quoted directly: 'I didn't want to lose the procurement. I said, "I want to split them out. I want them to be two different ballot measures."' He argued the narrower, standalone measure would help the City 'complete projects faster and avoid contractors inflating bids' due to unpriced risk under the current lowest-bidder-only system.

On July 14, 2026, the Santa Clara City Council voted unanimously, 7-0, to place this narrower version of the public-works measure on the November 2026 ballot, after setting aside the broader Charter package; Jain, as one of the seven councilmembers, was part of that unanimous vote per the City Attorney's Impartial Analysis and the Local News Matters report on the Council's decision. The primary argument in favor of Measure C that Jain filed was co-signed by Councilmember Karen Hardy (District 3), Vice Mayor Albert Gonzalez (District 1), and two members of the Charter Review Committee signing as individual voters.

I was not able to independently verify Jain's pre-council career, education, prior public offices, the year he first joined the Council, committee assignments, or specific named votes beyond Measure C and the Council's unanimous vote to place it on the ballot. This session's WebSearch tool had exhausted its query budget and firecrawl had exhausted its credit budget before this profile was researched, and direct WebFetch attempts at the City of Santa Clara's official council and district-5 pages (santaclaraca.gov) returned 403 Forbidden responses throughout this session; a Local News Matters article that likely contained further biographical or Council-meeting detail was behind that outlet's registration wall and could not be read. Because of that, years_of_service, committee_memberships, and endorsements_received are left empty or omitted below rather than populated with unverified claims.
voting_record_highlights: Measure C (2026), City of Santa Clara public-works Charter amendment: Jain was the lead author and filer of the primary argument in favor, and was one of seven councilmembers who voted unanimously (7-0) on July 14, 2026 to place the measure on the November 2026 ballot after the Council set aside a broader, comprehensive Charter overhaul. (Source: City of Santa Clara City Attorney's Impartial Analysis of Measure C; Local News Matters, 'Santa Clara scales back charter proposal, sends public works measure to voters.')
attendance: No individually published meeting-attendance or voting-participation record for Councilmember Jain was found. The City of Santa Clara does not appear to publish a per-member attendance scorecard on its public-facing pages; City Council meeting minutes and agendas are available via the city's Legistar/agenda system, which would in principle allow a manual tally of attendance and votes, but compiling that was not feasible within this session's tool budget (WebSearch and firecrawl both exhausted, and direct fetches of santaclaraca.gov returned 403 Forbidden throughout this session).
